title: Does the osrobot-uav multirotor energy model match real aircraft?
summary: Checks the osrobot-uav multirotor power model (imported unchanged) against two aircraft with a published mass, pack energy and endurance: DJI Mavic 3E (1.050 kg, 77 Wh, 45 min) and Parrot Anafi UKR (1.450 kg, 78.5 Wh, 38 min at 21.6 km/h), taken from Wikipedia's specification tables. Rotor diameter is not in the sources, so it is swept from 0.15 to 0.30 m: the model's endurance over the published one runs from 0.68 to 2.21 (Mavic) and 0.47 to 1.47 (Anafi). The model matches the published endurance at 0.181 m (Mavic) and 0.248 m (Anafi) at 90 % usable energy. At 0.22 m the errors have opposite signs (1.31× and 0.85×). Two aircraft of one class only; the fixed-wing and VTOL models are not tested; figures are from a secondary source and manufacturer maxima. Update: DJI's listing gives the Mavic 3 propellers as 9.4 in (0.239 m); at that diameter the model gives 1.30 to 1.63× the published endurance (80 to 100 % usable), so the earlier matching diameter of 0.18 m was a fit to a wrong model, not a rotor size. The Anafi diameter is still unsourced.
